examples.en: I ordered fried dumplings at the Chinese restaurant.
I dip fried dumplings in soy sauce.
The kids only ate the fried dumplings and left the jjajangmyeon.

examples.ko: 여기 군만두 한 접시 더 주세요.
examples.en: One more plate of fried dumplings here, please.

examples.ko: 집에서 만든 군만두가 가게 것보다 맛있어요.
examples.en: Homemade fried dumplings taste better than the ones from the shop.

explain: 기름에 구워 겉이 바삭한 만두예요. 쪄서 먹는 '찐만두', 삶아서 먹는 '물만두'와 비교해서 알아 두면 좋아요. 중국집에서 '군만두 하나 주세요'라고 자주 주문해요.

phrases.en: I ordered fried dumplings and ate them for dinner.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식을 주문할 때 '시키다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 시키다 is used for ordering food.

phrases.en: One more order of fried dumplings, please.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당에서 수를 말하며 주문할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to order by quantity at a restaurant.

phrases.en: The crispy fried dumplings are really delicious.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉이 바삭한 맛을 말할 때 '바삭한'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: 바삭한 describes the crispy outside.

explain_en: These are dumplings pan-fried in oil until the outside is crispy. It helps to compare them with '찐만두' (steamed) and '물만두' (boiled). At Chinese restaurants people often order with '군만두 하나 주세요'.

examples.en: In summer, a cold melon is really delicious.
Would you like a slice of melon for dessert?
I bought two melons at the market.

examples.ko: 이 멜론은 아주 달고 향이 좋아요.
examples.en: This melon is very sweet and smells great.
I ordered a melon juice at the cafe.
The melon isn't ripe yet, so it's still hard.

explain: 멜론은 껍질에 그물 무늬가 있고 크고 달콤한 과일이에요. 한국에서는 노란 참외도 여름에 많이 먹어요. '멜론 한 조각', '멜론을 자르다'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 저는 후식으로 멜론 한 조각을 먹었어요.
phrases.en: I ate a slice of melon for dessert.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘라 놓은 멜론을 셀 때는 '조각'을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 조각 to count cut pieces of melon.

phrases.en: Grandmother cut the melon in half.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과일을 먹기 전에 자를 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for cutting fruit before eating.

phrases.en: I ordered melon juice at the cafe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 멜론으로 만든 음료를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A drink made from melon.

explain_en: A melon is a large, sweet fruit with a netted rind. In Korea, the yellow 참외 (Korean melon) is also eaten a lot in summer. It is used as '멜론 한 조각' (a slice of melon) and '멜론을 자르다' (cut a melon).

examples.ko: 주말 아침마다 가족에게 팬케이크를 구워 줘요.
examples.en: Every weekend morning I make pancakes for my family.

examples.ko: 따뜻한 팬케이크 위에 꿀을 듬뿍 뿌렸어요.
examples.en: I drizzled plenty of honey on the warm pancakes.

examples.ko: 이 카페는 팬케이크가 두껍고 아주 푹신해요.
examples.en: This cafe's pancakes are thick and very fluffy.
I ate all three pancakes.

examples.ko: 우유와 달걀로 팬케이크 반죽을 만들고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm making pancake batter with milk and eggs.

explain: 한국에서는 '핫케이크'라는 말도 같이 써요. 집에서 만드는 가루 제품 이름이 보통 '핫케이크 가루'라서 장 볼 때는 핫케이크를 더 많이 보고, 카페 메뉴에서는 팬케이크가 많아요. 한국 사람들은 보통 '팬케이크 한 장'처럼 '장'으로 세어요.

phrases.en: I bought pancake mix at the mart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 팬케이크와 같은 뜻이고, 마트의 가루 제품에서 더 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as pancake; more common on mix products in stores.

phrases.en: I made pancakes this morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집에서 만들 때는 '굽다'를 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 굽다 (to bake/grill) when you make them at home.

phrases.en: I ate a whole pancake.
phrases.nuance_ko: 납작한 팬케이크는 '장'으로 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Flat pancakes are counted with 장.

explain_en: Koreans also say '핫케이크'. The mixes sold for home cooking are usually labeled '핫케이크 가루', so you see 핫케이크 more when shopping, while cafe menus tend to say 팬케이크. You count them with '장', as in '팬케이크 한 장'.

examples.en: I took my time looking at paintings at the art museum.
Listening to music is my hobby.
Please enjoy it quietly for the sake of others.
We talked after watching the performance.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날 창밖 풍경을 감상하면서 커피를 마셨어요.
examples.en: On a rainy day I drank coffee while taking in the view out the window.

explain: 영화, 음악, 그림, 공연처럼 즐기면서 보고 듣는 대상에 써요. 일상적인 것에는 그냥 '보다', '듣다'를 써요. 취미를 말할 때 '영화 감상', '음악 감상'이라고 짧게 말하는 것도 아주 흔해요.

phrases.en: My hobby is watching movies.
phrases.nuance_ko: 취미를 말할 때 '감상'을 명사로 붙여 짧게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a noun to name a hobby in a short way.

phrases.example: 저는 자기 전에 음악 감상을 해요.
phrases.en: I listen to music before I go to sleep.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음악을 즐기며 듣는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for listening to music for enjoyment.

phrases.en: I looked at paintings at the art museum yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형으로, 즐기면서 본 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form, used for something enjoyed by looking or listening.

explain_en: Use it for things you watch or listen to for enjoyment: films, music, paintings, performances. For everyday seeing and hearing, just use '보다' and '듣다'. When talking about hobbies, short answers like '영화 감상' and '음악 감상' are very common.

examples.en: We played dodgeball at the playground with a small rubber ball.

examples.ko: 고무공은 땅에 떨어지면 높이 튀어 올라요.
examples.en: A rubber ball bounces high when it hits the ground.
The puppy ran over with the rubber ball in its mouth.
The rubber ball flew over the fence.
I got hit by a rubber ball, but it didn't hurt as much as I thought.
I bought a rubber ball at the mart too.

explain: 고무로 만든 공이라서 통통 튀는 느낌이 있어요. '축구공, 농구공'처럼 경기 이름이 붙은 공과 달리 놀이용 공을 말할 때 잘 어울려요. '고무공이 통통 튀다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: The rubber ball bounces on the floor.
phrases.nuance_ko: '통통'은 공이 튀는 소리와 모양을 흉내 내는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 통통 imitates the sound and motion of a bouncing ball.

phrases.en: The child threw the rubber ball to a friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공을 손으로 던지는 놀이를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for throwing a ball by hand in play.

phrases.en: We played with a rubber ball in the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)로'는 놀이 도구를 나타낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: -(으)로 marks the tool you play with.

explain_en: Because it is made of rubber, it has a bouncy feel. Unlike balls named after a sport, such as '축구공' and '농구공', it fits a play ball. You say things like '고무공이 통통 튀다' (the rubber ball bounces).

examples.en: I colored the drawing with a felt-tip pen.
The felt-tip pen dried out and won't write.
Felt-tip pens bleed, so be careful when you use them.
I bought a set of felt-tip pens at the stationery store.
I put one felt-tip pen in my bag.

explain: 영어로는 보통 felt-tip pen이라고 해요. '펜'은 볼펜, 만년필까지 넓게 가리키지만 '사인펜'은 끝이 부드러운 펜이에요. 세는 말은 '자루'를 많이 써요.

phrases.en: I wrote my name with a felt-tip pen.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도구를 나타내는 '-로'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with -로 to show the tool.
phrases.en_equiv: to write with a felt-tip pen

phrases.en: I bought one felt-tip pen at the stationery store.
phrases.nuance_ko: 펜은 '자루'로 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pens are counted with 자루.

phrases.en: Can you lend me a black felt-tip pen?
phrases.nuance_ko: 색을 앞에 붙여 어떤 펜인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a color in front to specify the pen.

explain_en: In English it is usually called a felt-tip pen. '펜' covers ballpoints and fountain pens too, but '사인펜' is the soft-tipped kind. The counter word is often '자루'.

examples.en: I folded paper cranes out of colored paper.
I cut the colored paper into circles and made a card.
Could you lend me one sheet of colored paper?
Colored paper is sold at stationery stores.
The glue smeared on the colored paper and made it messy.
I need colored paper for art class today.

explain: '색종이를 접다', '색종이를 오리다', '색종이를 붙이다'처럼 손으로 만드는 활동과 같이 나와요. 크고 두꺼운 그림용 종이인 '도화지'와는 달라요. 종이접기를 할 때 특히 많이 써요.

phrases.en: The children folded colored paper and made airplanes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종이접기를 할 때 가장 많이 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation for origami activities.

phrases.en: I cut out colored paper with scissors and make flowers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가위로 모양대로 자를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when cutting shapes out with scissors.

phrases.en: I stuck colored paper onto drawing paper and finished the picture.
phrases.nuance_ko: 풀로 붙여서 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when gluing paper to decorate something.

explain_en: It appears with hands-on activities, as in '색종이를 접다' (fold), '색종이를 오리다' (cut out) and '색종이를 붙이다' (stick). It differs from '도화지', the larger, thicker drawing paper. It is especially common for origami.

examples.en: I got a free sample at the cosmetics shop.
I'll try the sample first and then buy.

examples.ko: 이 샘플은 무료이고 한 사람에게 하나만 줘요.
examples.en: This sample is free and we give only one per person.

examples.ko: 음악 샘플을 먼저 들어 보고 결정하세요.
examples.en: Listen to the music sample first and then decide.

examples.ko: 새 제품 샘플이 우리 회사에 도착했어요.
examples.en: Samples of the new product arrived at our company.

examples.ko: 설문 조사에 쓸 샘플 데이터를 모았어요.
examples.en: I collected sample data to use in the survey.

explain: 가게에서 맛이나 향을 먼저 보라고 주는 작은 제품과 음악·디자인·데이터의 일부 견본이 모두 샘플이에요. '시식'은 먹어 보는 행동이고 샘플은 그 물건이라 달라요. '견본'은 서류나 공장 이야기에서 더 딱딱하게 들려요.

phrases.en: You can take this sample product with you.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사기 전에 써 보라고 주는 작은 제품을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A small product given for trying before you buy.

phrases.en: I looked at the sample in the catalog.
phrases.nuance_ko: '샘플'과 뜻이 같지만 서류나 공장 이야기에서 더 딱딱하게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 'sample' but sounds more formal in documents or factory talk.

phrases.en: I tried a taste at the mart and then bought it.
phrases.nuance_ko: '시식'은 먹어 보는 행동이고 '샘플'은 그 물건이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 'Sishik' is the act of tasting, while 'sample' is the item itself.

explain_en: The small product a shop hands out to try, and a partial specimen of music, design or data, are all 'sample'. '시식' is the act of tasting, while the sample is the item itself. '견본' sounds stiffer and shows up in paperwork or factory talk.

t90.ax: I'll try the sample first and then buy.

examples.en: The glass cup broke. Be careful.
I put ice in the glass cup and poured juice.

examples.ko: 아이가 있어서 유리컵 대신 플라스틱 컵을 써요.
examples.en: We have a child, so we use plastic cups instead of glass ones.
I almost cut my hand while washing a glass cup.
I bought three new glass cups.

examples.ko: 뜨거운 물을 부으면 유리컵이 깨질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you pour hot water in, the glass cup can break.

explain: 종이컵, 플라스틱 컵, 머그컵과 구분해서 재료를 말할 때 써요. 컵은 '개'로 세요. 깨지기 쉬운 물건이라 '깨지다', '조심하다'와 자주 같이 나와요.

phrases.en: Please give me just two glasses.
phrases.nuance_ko: 컵은 '개'로 세어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Cups are counted with 'gae'.

phrases.en: I put the juice in a glass cup.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음료나 음식을 컵에 넣을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when putting a drink or food in a cup.

phrases.en: Wrap a broken glass in newspaper and throw it away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깨진 상태를 꾸며 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the broken state.

explain_en: Use it to specify the material, as opposed to a paper cup, plastic cup, or mug. You count cups with '개'. Since it's fragile, it often appears with '깨지다' (to break) and '조심하다' (to be careful).

examples.en: The children floated paper boats in the stream.
Please show me how to fold a paper boat.
A paper boat sinks quickly once it gets wet.
My child likes playing with paper boats.

explain: '종이배를 접다', '종이배를 띄우다'처럼 짝이 되는 말과 같이 외우면 좋아요. 종이로 접어 만드는 놀이라서 '색종이', '종이비행기'와 같이 나와요. 어린 시절 이야기에서 자주 쓰여요.

phrases.en: I folded a paper boat with my child.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종이배를 만드는 과정을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the act of making a paper boat.

phrases.en: I floated a paper boat on the water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 만든 배를 물에 놓을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you set the boat on the water.

phrases.en: A paper boat is floating on the pond.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종이배가 물 위에 있는 모습을 그릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a paper boat sitting on the water.

explain_en: It helps to learn it with its partner verbs, as in '종이배를 접다' (fold) and '종이배를 띄우다' (float). Since it's folded from paper, it appears alongside '색종이' (colored paper) and '종이비행기' (paper plane). It often shows up in childhood stories.

examples.ko: 문장 끝에 느낌표를 붙이면 감정이 더 잘 보여요.
examples.en: If you add an exclamation mark at the end, the feeling shows more.

examples.ko: 친구가 메시지마다 느낌표를 열 개씩 보내요.
examples.en: My friend sends ten exclamation marks in every message.

examples.ko: 느낌표 대신 물결표를 쓰는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people use a tilde instead of an exclamation mark.

examples.ko: 시험 문제에 느낌표가 들어간 문장이 있었어요.
examples.en: There was a sentence with an exclamation mark in the test question.

examples.ko: 느낌표가 너무 많으면 화난 것처럼 보일 수 있어요.
examples.en: Too many exclamation marks can look like you're angry.

examples.ko: 인사말 끝에는 느낌표를 써서 밝게 보여요.
examples.en: Put an exclamation mark at the end of a greeting to look cheerful.

explain: 한국어에서 느낌표는 반갑거나 놀라거나 강하게 말하는 느낌을 더해요. 공식 문서나 편지에서는 많이 쓰지 않아요. 메시지에서는 '!!'처럼 여러 개를 쓰는 사람도 많아요.

phrases.example: 메시지에 느낌표를 쓰면 더 반가워 보여요.
phrases.en: If you use an exclamation mark in a message, it looks friendlier.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글에 느낌표를 넣는 행동을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about putting an exclamation mark in writing.

phrases.en: We write a question mark or an exclamation mark at the end of a sentence.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문장 부호를 함께 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pair used when talking about punctuation marks together.

phrases.en: There are too many exclamation marks in my friend's messages.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이/가'를 붙여 느낌표의 양을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses 이/가 to talk about how many exclamation marks there are.

explain_en: In Korean an exclamation mark adds a feeling of gladness, surprise or emphasis. It isn't used much in official documents or letters. In messages many people use several, like '!!'.

examples.en: Read the passage above and answer the following questions.
I answered the teacher's question right away.

examples.ko: 그는 속내를 드러내기 싫어서 질문에 답하지 않았어요.
examples.en: He didn't want to reveal his feelings, so he didn't answer the question.
It takes a while to reply to the email.

examples.ko: 어떻게 답할지 몰라서 잠깐 가만히 있었어요.
examples.en: I didn't know how to answer, so I stayed quiet for a moment.

examples.ko: 면접에서 질문에 침착하게 답하는 연습을 했어요.
examples.en: I practiced answering questions calmly in an interview.

explain: '대답하다'와 거의 같지만, '답하다'는 시험 문제, 설문, 글처럼 글로 된 질문에 많이 나와요. 짝말은 '묻다'이고, 편지나 메시지에 답할 때는 '답장하다'도 써요. 사람에게 말할 때는 '~에게 답하다', 질문에는 '~에 답하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Please answer the question.
phrases.nuance_ko: 설문이나 시험처럼 정중하게 요청할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite request, as in surveys or exams.

phrases.en: My friend answered my question right away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻이에요. 사람과 말할 때는 대답하다가 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning; sounds more natural when talking with a person.

phrases.en: I replied to my friend's message right away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 편지나 메시지에 답할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when replying to a letter or message.

explain_en: It is almost the same as '대답하다', but '답하다' often appears with written questions such as test items, surveys and texts. Its counterpart is '묻다', and for letters or messages you can also say '답장하다'. Use '~에게 답하다' for a person and '~에 답하다' for a question.

t90.ax: It takes a while to reply to the email.

examples.en: Put a question mark at the end of the sentence.

examples.ko: 물음표가 있으면 질문이라는 걸 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: If there's a question mark, you can tell it's a question.

examples.ko: 편지 끝에 물음표를 세 개나 썼어요.
examples.en: I wrote three question marks at the end of the letter.
The question mark is missing from this sentence.

examples.ko: 물음표 대신 느낌표를 쓰면 느낌이 달라져요.
examples.en: If you use an exclamation mark instead of a question mark, the feeling changes.

examples.ko: 한국어는 물음표 없이도 말끝을 올려서 질문해요.
examples.en: In Korean you can ask a question by raising the end of the sentence, even without a question mark.

explain: 문장 부호는 '마침표(.), 쉼표(,), 느낌표(!), 물음표(?)'예요. 한국어 질문은 말로는 '-요?' 끝을 올려서 만들고, 글에서는 물음표를 붙여요. 발음은 [무름표]예요.

phrases.en: to raise doubts about something
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일이 맞는지 의심하거나 질문을 제기할 때 써요. 뉴스나 글에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when people question whether something is right. It appears often in news and writing.

explain_en: The main punctuation marks are 마침표, 쉼표, 느낌표 and 물음표. Spoken questions rise on the ending like '-요?', and in writing you add a 물음표. It is pronounced [무름표].

examples.en: Ouch! My finger got caught hard in the door.
Ow, what are you doing stepping on my foot?

examples.ko: 주사를 맞을 때 아야 소리가 나왔어요.
examples.en: I let out an ouch when I got the shot.
My younger sibling fell and cried out ouch.
Ouch, it's so hot! I burned my hand.

examples.ko: 아야, 머리를 세게 부딪쳤는데 괜찮아 보여요?
examples.en: Ow, I hit my head hard. Do I look okay?

explain: 갑자기 아플 때 짧게 나오는 소리예요. 어른은 '아!', '아이고', '아우'도 많이 쓰고, '아야'는 아이들 말 같은 느낌이 조금 있어요. 계속 아픈 것을 설명할 때는 소리 대신 '아파요'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Ouch, my back!
phrases.nuance_ko: 어른들이 아프거나 힘들 때 많이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adults often say this when in pain or feeling worn out.

phrases.en: Ow, it's hot!
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 아프거나 뜨거울 때 나오는 짧은 소리예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short sound when something suddenly hurts or is hot.

phrases.en: My head hurts.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리 대신 아픈 것을 설명할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe pain in words instead of a sound.

explain_en: It is the short sound that comes out at a sudden pain. Adults often use '아!', '아이고' or '아우' too, and '아야' has a slightly childlike feel. To explain ongoing pain, use '아파요' instead of the sound.

examples.ko: 훈민정음이 만들어지기 전에는 한자를 빌려 우리말을 적었어요.
examples.en: Before Hunminjeongeum was created, people wrote our language by borrowing Chinese characters.

examples.ko: 아이 이름을 지으려고 예쁜 우리말을 찾아보고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for pretty Korean words to name my child.

examples.ko: 외국인 친구가 우리말을 정말 잘해서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: My foreign friend speaks Korean so well that I was surprised.

examples.ko: 이 영어 표현을 우리말로 어떻게 하면 좋을까요?
examples.en: How should we say this English expression in Korean?

examples.ko: 요즘 우리말에 영어 단어가 너무 많이 섞여 있어요.
examples.en: These days there are too many English words mixed into Korean.

examples.ko: 우리말의 높임 표현은 외국인에게 조금 어려워요.
examples.en: Honorific expressions in Korean are a little hard for foreigners.

explain: '한국어'와 같은 언어를 가리키지만 '우리말'은 한국 사람이 자기 말을 가깝게 부르는 느낌이 있어요. 외국어와 비교할 때나 순우리말(고유어)을 이야기할 때 자주 나와요. 외국인이 자기 입장에서 말할 때는 보통 '한국어'를 써요.

phrases.en: How do you say this word in our language?
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 나라 말과 비교하며 뜻을 물을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when asking for a meaning in comparison with another language.

phrases.en: 'Haneul' is a native Korean word.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한자어나 외래어가 아닌 원래 한국의 말을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to original Korean words, not Sino-Korean or loanwords.

phrases.en: I'm learning Korean.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '한국어'처럼 편하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual everyday way to say 'Korean language'.

explain_en: It refers to the same language as '한국어', but '우리말' sounds closer, as Koreans talking about their own language. It often appears when comparing with foreign languages or talking about native Korean words. Foreigners speaking from their own side usually say '한국어'.
